results.hypothesis: To empirically test whether higher feature selection stability, as measured by the Consistency Index, correlates with higher downstream test accuracy in NLP text classification tasks using the AG News dataset.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Random feature selection without stability considerations
results.success_criteria: A positive correlation between Consistency Index scores and test accuracy would support the hypothesis. Conversely, no correlation or negative correlation would refute it.
results.notes: Correlation coefficient: 1.0000. Positive correlation indicates support for hypothesis.

results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.

assumptions_made: Used a fixed number of bootstrap samples (20) rather than adaptive sampling based on convergence
Applied feature selection using chi2 statistic with a fixed K (1000) rather than optimizing K
Used logistic regression as the classifier with default parameters rather than tuning hyperparameters
Calculated consistency index as frequency of feature appearance across bootstrap samples rather than more complex similarity measures
Used a simple split of features into high/low consistency rather than more sophisticated clustering approaches
Did not implement early stopping for training due to time constraints, assuming sufficient epochs for convergence
